newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rising Bunds have 99.00 in their sights.
newsitem.headline: Rising Bunds have 99.00 in their sights.

text.p: German Bunds chalked up strong gains in late trade on Tuesday, lifted by a rise in U.S. Treasuries following a stronger-than-expected fall in the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management index (NAPM).
December Bund futures were quoted at 98.96 at 1437 GMT, up 34 basis points from Monday's close, and had the 99.00 level in their sights, dealers said.
"The U.S. market is setting the trend for us," one Frankfurt-based Bund dealer said. "We'll see 99.00, if not today then tomorrow. The market wants to rise."

Treasuries rose following news the NAPM index, viewed as a key indicator of the economy's performance, fell to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August. A reading above 50 indicates an expanding economy, while one below 50 indicates a slowdown.

The report was slightly weaker than forecast by Wall Street economists, and the inflation-sensitive 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained about a third of a point, pulling its yield down to 6.90 percent from 6.92 percent late Monday.
Bunds had risen to modest gains earlier in the session after support at the day's low of 98.58 held, prompting short-covering.
Bunds showed little reaction to news of strong growth in German industrial production in August. Output rose 0.8 percent from the previous month and rose 1.8 percent year-on-year.
"The German data were ignored, everybody is looking at the U.S. market this week. I think Bunds could rise to 99.10 ahead of Friday," one Frankfurt-based dealer said.
The market was also unmoved by U.S. August leading indicators, which were up 0.2 percent, in line with forecasts.
The market's next major focus is the U.S. September payrolls report due Friday.
